subprocess: Payroll System Access and Segregation of Duties
risk: A single person can create an employee, change pay details and release the payment, allowing fabricated employees or altered pay to reach the bank without detection.
audit_objective: Confirm that payroll system access is restricted by role and that no individual controls the full payroll cycle.
what_to_review: Role design and who holds each payroll role
Conflicting combinations — master data maintenance with payroll processing or payment release
Access of HR, Finance and IT staff to payroll data
Privileged and vendor support accounts
Access reviews and removal on transfer or exit
procedures: Extract all users with payroll system access and map their roles against a segregation of duties matrix; quantify unmitigated conflicts.
Test whether any single user can both amend an employee record and approve the pay run, using the system rather than the policy as evidence.
Test that IT and vendor support accounts cannot post or release payroll transactions, and review their activity logs.
Trace payroll staff who changed role or left, and measure days to access removal.
Test whether the last access review was performed by the payroll owner and whether flagged removals actually happened.
red_flags: Emergency or firefighter access left permanently enabled
Shared accounts used at pay run time
Access reviews approved in bulk on one day
Support vendor with standing production access
evidence: Payroll system user and role listings
HR joiner, mover and leaver data

risk: Bank details, salary or employment status are changed without authorisation or verification, diverting pay or inflating it.
audit_objective: Verify that every change to employee master data is authorised, independently verified and traceable to a source document.
what_to_review: Authorisation and verification of salary, bank and status changes
Source documentation retained for each change
Change reporting and who reviews it
Duplicate bank accounts, addresses or tax identifiers
Changes made close to the pay run cut-off
procedures: Extract the full master data change log for the period and reconcile it to authorised change forms.
Test all bank detail changes for independent verification back to a source the employee did not supply alone.
Run duplicate analytics across bank account, address, national insurance or SIN, and email across the active population.
Analyse changes made within 48 hours of the pay run cut-off and test each for approval.
Test whether the change report is genuinely reviewed, by re-performing the review for one period.
red_flags: Bank change immediately followed by a pay increase
Multiple employees sharing one bank account
Changes entered and approved by the same user
Retrospective approval forms dated after the change
evidence: Master data change logs with user and timestamp

risk: The payroll is released without anyone reviewing the register against the prior period, so errors and fraudulent entries pass straight to the bank.
audit_objective: Confirm that the payroll register is reviewed on a meaningful basis and authorised by someone independent before payment.
what_to_review: Pre-payment review of the register and variance to prior period
Investigation thresholds for movements and new joiners
Authorisation limits and who signs the pay run
Exception reports — negative pay, duplicate payments, high net pay, zero deductions
Evidence retained of the review
procedures: For a sample of pay runs, obtain the register and the reviewer evidence; re-perform the period-on-period variance analysis and test whether flagged items were investigated.
Test that the authoriser is independent of payroll preparation and within their authority.
Re-perform the exception reports on the payroll data and test whether the same exceptions were identified and cleared.
Test the completeness of the register reviewed against the payment file actually transmitted to the bank.
red_flags: Sign-off dated after the payment was released
Variance review consisting of a total-only comparison
Exceptions cleared with the note "checked"
Register reviewed by the person who prepared it

risk: Hours paid are not the hours worked, because time records are entered, amended or approved by people who benefit from them.
audit_objective: Assess whether time and attendance data is captured accurately, approved independently and flows unaltered into pay.
what_to_review: Time capture method and its integrity — biometric, badge, manual sheets
Supervisor approval of hours and whether it is exercised
Amendments to submitted time records and who makes them
Buddy punching and remote clock-in controls
Interface integrity between the time system and payroll
procedures: Reconcile hours approved in the time system to hours paid in the register and investigate differences.
Analyse time record amendments by user; amendments by payroll or by the employee themselves warrant testing.
Test approval evidence for a sample of timesheets and identify approvals granted after the pay run.
Where clock-in is remote or app-based, test the location and device controls.
Analyse employees with implausible patterns — identical hours every period, hours exceeding shift length.
red_flags: Approvals granted in bulk seconds apart
Amendments concentrated with one supervisor
Employees clocked in at two locations
Manual timesheets replacing system capture for particular teams

risk: Overtime, shift premiums, bonuses and commissions are claimed and approved without support, or calculated on the wrong basis.
audit_objective: Confirm that variable pay is earned, supported, correctly calculated and approved within authority.
what_to_review: Overtime authorisation before it is worked, not after
Premium and allowance eligibility rules and their application
Bonus and commission calculation against plan rules
Approval authority and self-approval risk
Concentration by employee, supervisor and cost centre
procedures: Analyse overtime by employee and supervisor as a percentage of base pay; test the top decile to pre-approval and time records.
Recompute a sample of shift premiums and allowances against the eligibility rules in the agreement or policy.
Recompute a sample of bonus and commission payments against the plan and the approved performance outcome.
Test for supervisors approving their own or a related party's variable pay.
red_flags: Overtime approved after the period worked
The same employees at the top of the overtime list every period
Allowances continuing after the qualifying condition ended
Commission paid on cancelled or unpaid sales
evidence: Payroll register with pay element detail

risk: Statutory deductions are calculated on the wrong basis or remitted late, exposing the organisation to interest, penalties and employee claims.
audit_objective: Confirm that statutory deductions are correct, complete and remitted within the required deadlines.
what_to_review: Tax code and withholding table maintenance and update timing
Pension, social security and levy calculations
Remittance deadlines by jurisdiction and evidence of payment
Year-end reporting and employee statements
Treatment of benefits in kind and taxable allowances
procedures: Recompute statutory deductions for a sample of employees across pay bands and jurisdictions.
Test that withholding tables were updated on the statutory effective date, not later.
Agree remittances to the authority receipts and test the payment date against the deadline; quantify interest and penalties.
Test the treatment of benefits in kind, allowances and expense reimbursements for correct taxability.
Reconcile year-end statements to the payroll ledger.
red_flags: Penalties recurring period after period
Tables updated retrospectively after an authority query
Benefits paid through expenses to avoid tax
Reconciling differences at year end carried forward unexplained

risk: New starters are paid before onboarding is complete and leavers continue to be paid after their exit date, or receive settlements outside policy.
audit_objective: Confirm that pay starts and stops on the correct date and that final settlements are calculated and approved correctly.
what_to_review: Timeliness of new starter set-up and first payment accuracy
Leaver notification from HR to payroll and the cut-off applied
Final settlement components — notice, accrued leave, severance
Approval authority for settlements and ex gratia payments
Recovery of overpayments after exit
procedures: Reconcile the payroll population to the HR active employee list and investigate every difference in both directions.
For all leavers in the period, test that pay ceased on the exit date and recompute the final settlement.
Test severance and ex gratia payments to the approval authority matrix and to any settlement agreement.
Quantify overpayments to leavers and test the recovery outcome.
Test first-payment accuracy for a sample of new starters, including pro-rating.
red_flags: Payments continuing one or more periods after exit
Settlements approved by the departing employee's own manager alone
Overpayments written off without attempt at recovery
Leaver notifications arriving after the pay run repeatedly
kpis: Days from exit to payroll cut-off

risk: Accrued leave, long service and benefit liabilities are misstated because entitlement rules are applied inconsistently or balances are never verified.
audit_objective: Confirm that leave and benefit balances reflect entitlement and are accurately valued.
what_to_review: Entitlement rules by contract type and their configuration
Leave taken recorded against the balance
Carry-over, expiry and cap rules
Valuation basis for the accrual, including on-costs
Long service, sabbatical and other long-term benefit provisions
procedures: Recompute leave balances for a sample of employees from entitlement, accrual and leave taken.
Test that leave actually taken is recorded — compare rosters or absence records to leave deductions.
Test carry-over and expiry rules against policy and identify balances exceeding caps.
Recompute the accrual valuation including employer on-costs and agree to the ledger.
red_flags: Employees with balances far above the cap
Leave taken but never deducted from the balance
Accrual valued at current salary where policy requires otherwise
Manual adjustments to balances without approval

subprocess: Payroll Payment Execution and Bank Controls
risk: The payment file is altered between approval of the payroll and transmission to the bank, or payments are made from accounts outside treasury control.
audit_objective: Confirm that the amount authorised is the amount paid, and that payroll banking is controlled.
what_to_review: Integrity of the payment file between payroll and bank — hash totals, control counts
Authorisation of the payment file at the bank and dual release
Payroll bank account mandates and signatories
Manual, off-cycle and emergency payments
Returned and unpresented payments
procedures: Agree total value and record count on the approved register to the file transmitted to the bank for a sample of runs.
Test that release at the bank requires two approvers independent of payroll preparation.
Test all off-cycle and manual payments for authorisation and business reason.
Review returned payments and test where the funds were redirected.
Confirm payroll bank mandates against the approved signatory list.
red_flags: Payment file totals differing from the approved register
Off-cycle payments used routinely
Returned payments re-issued to a different account
Payroll accounts with signatories no longer employed
evidence: Bank payment files and transmission logs

risk: Payroll is outsourced but the risk is not, and the organisation cannot evidence that the provider's controls actually operate.
audit_objective: Assess whether an outsourced payroll arrangement is governed, assured and recoverable.
what_to_review: Contract terms — service levels, liability, audit rights, data protection
Assurance obtained, such as a service auditor report, and whether it is read
Complementary user entity controls the organisation must perform
Data transfer security and employee data protection
Exit and continuity planning if the provider fails
procedures: Obtain the provider's service auditor report; identify the complementary user controls and test whether the organisation actually performs each one.
Review report exceptions and test whether management assessed their impact.
Test the reconciliation performed on data returned by the provider before it is accepted.
Review the contract for audit rights and data protection terms, and test whether any audit has been exercised.
Assess the continuity plan for running payroll if the provider became unavailable.
red_flags: Service auditor report received but never opened
Complementary user controls not even identified
Provider output accepted without reconciliation
No plan for a pay run if the provider fails

subprocess: Payroll Reconciliation, Cost Analysis and Ghost Employees
risk: Payroll is not reconciled to the general ledger or to headcount, so fabricated employees and systematic errors persist undetected.
audit_objective: Confirm payroll costs reconcile to the ledger and to a verified workforce, and test for fictitious employees.
what_to_review: Reconciliation of payroll to the general ledger and to headcount
Cost per head and payroll cost trend analysis by department
Existence verification of employees
Employees with no leave taken, no deductions or no email account
Bank account and address matching across the population
procedures: Reconcile total payroll cost to the general ledger for each period and test unexplained differences.
Reconcile paid headcount to HR records and to an independent source such as building access or IT accounts; investigate every unmatched name.
Test for employees who never take leave, have no tax deductions, or share bank details with another employee.
For a sample of employees, verify existence through independent confirmation — line manager attestation, access records, or physical verification.
Analyse payroll cost per head by department against expectation.
red_flags: Employees with no system account and no leave history
Payroll to ledger differences carried as a rounding plug
Headcount reported by HR differing persistently from payroll
New employees created shortly before the pay run and removed after
evidence: Building access and IT account listings
